output.summary: The evidence does not support a pay-driven rise: pay was the top exit reason in both years, so it cannot explain the change, and no market benchmark exists since 2023. The HRIS-artifact claim is contradicted because payroll reconciles both years' separation counts. Cedar Hollow's rise (28% to 47%) far exceeds in-state peers (33% to 38%). Vacancy-driven overtime is well supported by policy-coded data. Branch-level separations are missing and manager data is stale, so the ShiftWise, Saturday and manager effects remain unresolved; ShiftWise branches were non-randomly selected. Do not approve the across-the-board raise or the manager bonus penalties yet. Produce corrected branch-level separations and a ShiftWise comparison first, before the December 1 and January 11 deadlines.
